S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major changes in working hours or conditions
patient_info.stressor: Johnathan’s symptoms began after a municipal groundskeeping contract changed his crew’s schedule to earlier starts, longer days, and more weekend coverage, leaving little room for the family meals, hikes, community garden work, and music gatherings that had kept his life balanced after divorce. At first he treated the heaviness and exhaustion as the price of responsibility, but over 3 years and 3 months the low mood, unrelieved fatigue, and growing hopelessness became woven into his daily routine. The condition became clinically significant when he could no longer reliably lead his crew, keep up with project planning, or maintain the community commitments that had defined him. He entered psychiatric care after an occupational health visit for declining work functioning led to a referral for evaluation.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: I’m here because most days I wake up already feeling like a gray weight is sitting on me, and even when I’m out with the crew or around my kids, I can’t shake this low, hollow feeling like I’m just going through the motions.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: By midmorning my body feels like I’ve already put in a full day, and even after sleeping on a Sunday I still drag through simple things like loading tools, checking job plans, or making dinner.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: I keep telling myself this is just how my life is now, like no matter how hard I work or try to get back to the garden or music nights, nothing is really going to turn around.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’ve started missing details on job planning, falling behind on crew paperwork, and avoiding the community garden and music gatherings I used to help organize, so people have had to step in where they used to count on me.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about 3 years and 3 months, since the groundskeeping contract changed our schedule and the longer days took over my life.
